"Can AI engines read and cite our site?"

Since launching, Akii has gained traction with small businesses, agencies, and brands for its freemium plan. Beyond the free AI Visibility Score, which guarantees users 100 monthly AI credits, Akii also offers a premium plan starting at $99 per month or $950 for the whole year. Akii is a Delaware-based AI search intelligence platform that shows marketers and business owners how AI models, such as ChatGPT and Google Gemini, perceive and rank their businesses. The AI visibility and optimization platform is designed to help businesses improve their discoverability on AI-driven search platforms. [...] As the world’s first free AI Visibility Score, Akii is revolutionizing brand intelligence and AI visibility for the AI-first internet. Akii AI Visibility Score scans AI models to see how brands rank across brand recognition, brand understanding, content coverage, and brand sentiment. Moreover, Akii is fast and easy to use. Users simply need to select the AI model they want to scan, enter their brand domain, and get results on their visibility in two minutes. The AI SEO tool provides a comprehensive report that shows brands their overall visibility score and a detailed analysis of their strengths, opportunities, and weaknesses across four key areas.

results.title: The Best AI Visibility Tools in 2026: 10 Picks (Free + Paid)
results.content:
Best for: small businesses, freelancers and anyone testing AI visibility before committing real budget.

Good alternative: Rankscale if you need lots of AI engines cheaply. It’s credit-based, starting at $17/month, billed yearly.

### 5. AthenaHQ: Best Engine Coverage for the Money

Most trackers cover three or four AI engines and charge extra for the rest. AthenaHQ goes the other way.

Its Starter plan covers 11 AI models, including ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews, AI Mode, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, Grok, DeepSeek, Meta AI and Mistral. And it has a genuinely free plan, Essential, which covers five engines with 300 credits. [...] Watch out for

The price, and the process. In September, Profound removed its $99 Starter and $399 Growth plans, leaving a free trial and custom Enterprise pricing. If you’re a small team, you’ll be talking to sales for a tool built for companies much bigger than yours.

Pricing: free trial, then custom Enterprise contracts. No published price.

Best for: large brands that treat AI visibility as a channel with its own budget and owner.

Good alternatives: Evertune (from $60/month) if statistical rigour matters most, since it samples each prompt many times per model. Brandlight if you want an enterprise platform with a more hands-on service model.

### 2. Peec AI: Best for Mid-Market Teams and Agencies

If Profound is the enterprise default, Peec AI is the default for everyone else. [...] What it’s good at

 Fixing what AI crawlers see, not just reporting on it.
 Spotting rendering and indexing issues that hide content from AI.
 Enterprise teams on Sitecore.

Watch out for

AXP is a separate layer built for machines. It can help, but it doesn’t fix the page your human visitors, or an AI agent using a real browser, actually land on. More on that in the next section.

Pricing: Starter from $250/month billed annually, or $300 month to month. 

Best for: larger sites with JavaScript-heavy pages that AI crawlers struggle to read.

Good alternative: Goodie (from $295/month) if you sell products. Its Agentic Commerce Suite tracks product-level visibility across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google’s AI Mode, Alexa for Shopping and Walmart’s Sparky.
